correctness.rationale: Within each strict sorting chamber, S is a coordinate permutation, so the global two-input Lipschitz constant equals the largest generalized norm of a permutation in A=I+γL_star. Every chamber is open; a small displacement along a generalized maximal eigenvector produces an actual attaining pair. Leaf permutations are A-isometries; moving the hub is conjugate to swapping hub with one leaf. The two-centered star matrices differ in rank two, their determinants are equal, and exact inversion gives trace defect δ=γ²(n²−1)/[(1+γ)(1+(n+1)γ)]. Thus the only nontrivial positive generalized eigenvalues have product 1 and sum 2+δ, yielding (sqrt(4+δ)+sqrtδ)/2. n=1 is isometric and γ→∞ yields the graph-Dirichlet quotient modulus (sqrt(n+3)+sqrt(n−1))/2. Fresh independent symmetric generalized eigenvalue calculations agreed for n=2..10 and γ=.1,1,3,9 (36 cases). The eigenvalue checks do not prove the all-n formula; the rank-two calculation does.
residual_risks: General weighted stars, nonlinear sorting conventions, and other Sobolev exponents are outside the proof.

value.rationale: Sorting is canonical and Euclidean nonexpansive, but data supported on a graph incur a non-permutation-invariant edge regularity penalty. The exact amplification factor on the simplest branching graph, all extremizing chambers, and √n strong-coupling asymptotics give a useful structural stability benchmark. In particular for n=2 homogeneous norm the factor is the golden ratio, not a routine restatement of rearrangement contraction.
residual_risks: Limited to unweighted stars and common γ, not arbitrary graphs.

limitations: Global TWO-input Lipschitz modulus; not one-input rearrangement-energy ratio.
